subject: Multi-year prepay: invoicing entity, FX exposure, VAT/GST & WHT — options and ramp
thread_text:
From: Luca Romano <luca.romano@zoomarket.io>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 9 Jul 2026 14:12:00 +0200
Subject: Multi‑year prepay — invoicing and tax points

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Zoomarket is excited by the latency/cost profile you showed. Before we move to legal/procurement we need to firm up a couple of invoicing and tax items so our finance and tax teams have clear guidance. Short list: 

- For a three‑year prepay with annual invoices, which Redwood entity issues the invoice for EU customers? Can you provide entity/legal name + VAT number options?
- FX exposure: can we invoice in EUR or must Redwood invoice in USD? If USD, what are options to fix FX (annual FX clause, hedge pass‑through, or invoice in EUR)?
- VAT/GST: will Zoomarket be charged VAT on Redwood invoices (we are VAT registered in Italy)? Any suggested flow for VAT reclaims or reverse charge applicability?
- Withholding tax: does Redwood have any routing that avoids foreign WHT (e.g., invoice from a local EU subsidiary vs Redwood US)?

Our procurement team would like a short note we can share internally — bullet points are fine. Also if you could attach the most recent draft MAP we discussed (pricing table + ramp schedule) that would be great.

Best,
Luca
Finance Operations — Zoomarket

--
Attachment: request_list.csv (stub)
From: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
To: Luca Romano <luca.romano@zoomarket.io>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:05:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Multi‑year prepay — invoicing and tax points

Hi Luca — thanks for the clear list. I pulled our tax/legal notes together and attached a short options memo plus the MAP draft you saw: Redwood_MultiYear_Options_v3.pdf and Signed-MAP-draft.docx (stubs). High level bullets below you can share with procurement: 

1) Invoicing entity options
   - Redwood EU BV (Luxembourg) — issues EUR invoices with EU VAT number; preferred for EU customers wanting euro billing.
   - Redwood Inc. (US) — issues USD invoices; used for customers who require Redwood US contracting.
   - For customers requiring local entity/legal contracting, we can evaluate routing via our EU entity for a committed contract (requires entity selection in PO).

2) FX exposure
   - Option A (EUR billing): Redwood EU BV invoices in EUR — Zoomarket sees no FX exposure.
   - Option B (USD billing): Redwood Inc. invoices in USD; add an FX clause in the MAP to define exchange rate handling (annual fix or monthly pass‑through).

3) VAT/GST
   - For B2B EU customers with valid VAT registration, the reverse charge normally applies if invoiced from an EU entity — no VAT charged on the invoice and customer self‑accounts.
   - If invoiced from Redwood Inc (US), VAT typically applies at import/OSS rules in some countries; tax team recommends EU invoicing where reverse charge is expected.

4) Withholding tax (WHT)
   - If Redwood EU BV invoices, most EU jurisdictions do not impose WHT on software SaaS cross‑border payments between EU entities.
   - Invoices from US entity can create WHT exposure in some jurisdictions — we recommend EU entity to avoid WHT where possible.

5) Practical recommendation
   - For a multi‑year EUR‑priced commitment, route invoices from Redwood EU BV and lock annual billed amounts in EUR. Add a small FX re‑opener only if >5% annual variance (optional).

Next steps: if that sounds OK I can loop in Legal for a one‑page invoicing addendum and share a revised MAP with explicit invoicing entity selected.

Evelyn Hart
Head of Deals, Redwood Inference
Attach: Redwood_MultiYear_Options_v3.pdf (pricing table + routing options)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Luca Romano <luca.romano@zoomarket.io>, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 11:22:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Multi‑year prepay — invoicing and tax points

Luca — quick note on discounts and ramp (so procurement sees numbers):

- Three‑year prepay (annual invoice at start of year): 18% term discount (year 1), 12% (year 2), 8% (year 3) relative to list, with 100% of committed spend invoiced up front each year.
- Ramp schedule option (if you prefer smoothing vs. annual step): split year 1 invoice into 60% upfront + 40% at month six; we can model this but it changes cash/cap accounting for both sides.
- If invoiced from EU entity, discount percentages are identical — only billing currency and tax flows change.

Also adding a small contractual clause option: if FX moves >7% vs agreed rate we can do an annual reconciliation (mutual agreement) — we find this avoids surprises while keeping pricing predictable.

Happy to jump on a 30‑minute call this week with your tax and AP teams — I can bring our tax lead (Marcus).

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Strategic Accounts
From: Luca Romano <luca.romano@zoomarket.io>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Cc: accounts-payable@zoomarket.io
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2026 16:47:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Multi‑year prepay — invoicing and tax points

Thanks for the clarity — that helps a lot. A couple follow ups from our tax/AP: 

- VAT: we will supply our Italian VAT number; please confirm you will apply reverse charge on EU BV invoices.
- WHT: our treasury team says their payment rails sometimes apply 10% WHT to US‑origin services unless local treaty relief is provided. If we select Redwood EU BV for invoicing, can you confirm this avoids the WHT exposure?
- FX clause: we prefer the annual reconciliation >7% approach. Please add sample language so our legal can review.

Can we schedule a 30‑minute sync Thursday 15 July 09:00 CEST with your tax lead (Marcus) and our AP? I can invite. 

Regards,
Luca

--
accounts-payable@zoomarket.io (CC)
From: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
To: Luca Romano <luca.romano@zoomarket.io>, accounts-payable@zoomarket.io
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 09:03:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Multi‑year prepay — invoicing and tax points

Luca — confirmed and thanks for the call invite. Quick answers before we meet: 

- VAT: yes — if we route the contract and invoices from Redwood EU BV we will issue invoices without VAT under the reverse charge regime for Italian VAT‑registered entities (we will include our EU VAT number on invoices).
- WHT: invoicing from Redwood EU BV should remove typical US‑origin WHT concerns; Marcus will bring our tax note that summarizes treaty positions commonly relied upon.
- FX clause: attached is suggested sample language in the MAP addendum (see Redwood_MultiYear_Options_v3.pdf). We will follow the annual >7% reconciliation approach.

Meeting confirmed 15 Jul 09:00 CEST — calendar invite sent. Looking forward to closing this — if AP needs a billing contact for the EU entity prior to signature please use: billing-eu@redwood.ai.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Deals, Redwood Inference
